newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA'S Grenville appointed deputy governor.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA'S Grenville appointed deputy governor.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Tuesday that Reserve Bank Assistant Governor (Economic) Stephen Grenville had been appointed as one of the bank's two deputy governors, filling a vacancy left by the elevation of Ian Macfarlane to the position of governor.

"I am pleased to announce that His Excellency the Governor-General (Sir William Deane) has appointed Dr Stephen Grenville as Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of Australia for a term of five years commencing December 1, 1996," Costello said in a statement.

Grenville, born in 1943, has worked in the bank since 1982, having previously followed a diplomatic career with the Foreign Affairs Department, including a stint as first secretary in the Saigon embassy in 1970 and 1971.

He later worked with the International Monetary Fund in Jakarta and with the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development in Paris. He was head of the bank's economic analysis department from in 1988, before his appointment as an assistant governor in 1992.
The bank has two deputy governors -- one post responsible for economic conditions and the other, held by Graeme Thompson, covering supervision of the banking system.
